### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **3** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json babda9d339b6e7c1ab0a527917edc2e8fb827bce` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `71f3a00e36602d555c3c900349c4d84d58442e1f` — the merge of head `84e37cabec247f97fd422aa5bab72b37438f42a5` into base `babda9d339b6e7c1ab0a527917edc2e8fb827bce`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 71f3a00e36602d555c3c900349c4d84d58442e1f && git checkout 71f3a00e36602d555c3c900349c4d84d58442e1f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin babda9d339b6e7c1ab0a527917edc2e8fb827bce 84e37cabec247f97fd422aa5bab72b37438f42a5 && git checkout -B drift-repro babda9d339b6e7c1ab0a527917edc2e8fb827bce && git merge --no-ff 84e37cabec247f97fd422aa5bab72b37438f42a5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json babda9d339b6e7c1ab0a527917edc2e8fb827bce
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs babda9d339b6e7c1ab0a527917edc2e8fb827bce` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `84e37cabec247f97fd422aa5bab72b37438f42a5`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/inbound-hook-disabled-holder-33906.test.ts + packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/plugin.ts, packages/triggers/trigger-api/src/api-trigger.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts, packages/core/src/security/inbound-hook-answer.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (`flowNameResolver`), packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-slots.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/flow-triggers-per-slot.test.ts:198-210, packages/spec/src/contracts/trigger-api-service.ts, docs/adr/0150 (D3, D5), skills/objectstack-automation/SKILL.md:383-395 (all read in the cited code, none in the diff)

Read: card #33906 with its five comments (measurement 6897225218, ruling 6898449441, regrade 6898457477, claim 6903498595, dev report 6906551199), ruling 6884403301 as data, PR #34278 body and three files, the net diff against `main` (`01598d93`, merge-base `98a4449f`; `engine.ts` on `main` differs from the head by this PR's hunk alone), and the 52 check-runs on the head: 36 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set of the door, sole-holder branch** (`inboundHookSlot`, `!isShared`): was `undefined` for every such name; now `unadmitted` when the name's one slot has a package and `isDisabledHolderSlot(name, package)` holds, else `undefined` as before. Right. A package-less slot, a name with no slot, and an engine with no resolver all keep `undefined` (`flowSlotPackage` answers `undefined`, or the predicate answers `false`).
- **Accept-set of the door, shared-name branch**: was `served` whenever the qualified address picked exactly one key; now `unadmitted` when that key's package is disabled. Right. The check runs after the pick on the picked key, so no other holder is substituted (amendment 8); `_env` picks the package-less slot and stays `served`; the bare hook returns `refused` above the new code and is untouched; zero or two keys stay `unadmitted`.
- **Key shapes**: `flowSlotPackage(flowName)` reads the bare key of an unshared name (after `settleFlowName` folds a lone qualified key back), and `flowSlotPackage(keys[0])` reads a `PACKAGE/NAME` key from `keysOf(flowName)`. Both return the slot's own `packageId`. Right.
- **Same predicate as the fire-time skip**: both branches call `isDisabledHolderSlot(bare name, slot package)`, the argument order `triggerRun` uses (`slot.name`, `slot.packageId`) and `isDisabledSoleHolder` uses. The door now refuses exactly the slots whose queued run `triggerRun` skips on `main`; it refuses no post that would have run. Right.
- **Callers**: three, none changed. Self-hosted bare and qualified mounts hand any non-`undefined` answer to `answerInboundHookSlot`, which reads the body and answers the trigger's refusal. The `trigger-api` member does the same for the hosted bare hook. The hosted qualified face answers `refuseUnaddressed` (body read, `inboundHookRefusalResponse()`) for any answer that is not `served`. No caller reads the former `undefined` of a sole holder in another way; the only behaviour that moves is the intended one. Right.
- **Sender-visible surface**: status, the one `Content-Type` header and the body are the door's existing `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE`. Nothing in them names the package, the namespace or the disabled state; the cause is in the engine's `info` line only. The `503` residual and the `400` body arms sit behind the hook match, so a disabled holder no longer reaches them, as after the re-sync. Right.
- **Post-time question**: `isDisabledHolderSlot` asks the resolver on every call and stores nothing; `disabledHolderDispatchSaid` is not touched. The enable answers `202` with no re-arm. Right.
- **Public surface**: no export, type or return union changes (`unadmitted` was already a member); the lint-gate and type-check runs are green. `disabledHolderHookRefused` is private. Right.
- **Pins**: the new file drives both faces with correctly signed posts and compares whole answers to `inboundHookRefusalResponse()` and to the post-`withdrawFlowSlot` answer. It lives in `@objectstack/dogfood`, whose shards run on the queue and on push, never on a pull request (`ci.yml`, the `dogfood` job's `if:`), so `Dogfood Regression Gate` is green here with its three shards skipped. No check-run on this head executed the file; its green reading is the dev's local battery (470 files, exit 0) and its first CI run is the queue build. `Test Core` (8 shards) is green, which covers `flow-triggers-per-slot.test.ts:198-210` (a toggled-off slot still routes `served`) and the existing `inboundHookSlot` pins.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/service-automation` is right: the only published source the diff moves is `engine.ts`, and AGENTS.md step 3 gives `Metadata-protocol: none` a `patch`, with a breaking non-protocol change keeping its banner and its ADR-0087 disposition. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes.
- `!` in the title and the BREAKING banner are present in the PR body and the changeset, with the corrected sender sentence of ruling 6898449441 and the remedy (enable the package).
- ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right: no key, export, stored row, slot key or secret moves, and the state is reversible. One marker, in the changeset body, beside both declaration lines.
- `trigger-api` and `runtime` carry no changeset and need none: their sources are unchanged.
- `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards` and `Lint · repo & tooling gates` are success on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing). Correct as declared: a sender-visible answer moves from `202` to `401` for the affected addresses.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty. `security_findings`: none; this review found none either (see ④).
- Deviation, test placement in `packages/qa/dogfood`: accepted. It is the one package that reaches the engine, the trigger plugin and the runtime dispatcher together. Its cost is stated in ①: no pull-request check-run runs it.
- Deviation, ablations at `aa16cc6e`: accepted. The `#33906` hunk of `engine.ts` is identical there and at the head (compared; the file otherwise differs only by an unrelated start-condition change merged from `main`). The pin file changed after the ablations by the read-only credential store alone.
- Deviation, other direct dependents left to CI: accepted; `Test Core` and the type-check runs are green.
- Deviation, the engine's cause line is per post, not once per slot: accepted. The door's own line is already per post, so the volume grows by a constant factor.
- Deviations on commit trailers, merge-commit messages and repo-wide lint: no contract effect; `Lint · ESLint` is green.
- Out-of-scope note, the door's generic cause: answered as N1 below. It has no carrier and one is owed.
- `Skills-docs: follow-up owed` for `SKILL.md:383-395`: the lines say the endpoint ACKs `202` and enqueues, and do not mention a disabled package. The request names #34279 as the carrier; this review did not open it.
- Not measured, stated by the dev: the full PATCH-disable stack through a booted app. The rig reaches the armed-but-disabled state with `registry.disablePackage` and no re-sync. Accepted as stated.

### ④ Design judgment

The change makes a declared refusal real; it takes no declared capability away. The published contract (`ITriggerApiService.handleInboundHook`) promises that a `202` means the payload is enqueued and the flow runs on the consumer, and gives every post that names no armed flow the one `401`. ADR-0150 D3 as the resolver reads it, and ruling 6884403301 amendment 3, say a disabled package's slot gets no flow and no dispatch. On `main` the door answers `202` and `triggerRun` then drops the run, so the sender is told a thing the contract does not allow. No spec text declares that a disabled package's hook is served. The door now gives the answer the same address gets once the re-sync has withdrawn the slot. This is seat ruling A (6898449441) as written: amendments 2, 3 and 8 are each met, ADR-0150 D5's one refusal is kept, and the bare hook of a shared name is left where PR #33646 left it.

Attempts to break it, each read in the tree:
- An environment-qualified address, a flow no package ships, and a toggled-off slot: unchanged, by `flowSlotPackage` answering `undefined` or the predicate answering `false`.
- A served co-holder whose slot stays alone under its qualified key beside a disabled, withdrawn co-holder: `isShared` stays true through `heldByMany`, the shared branch picks the served key, and it is `served`.
- A wrong-namespace or `_env` address of a disabled sole holder: `unadmitted` now, and the door's refusal before, the same bytes.
- Unauthenticated learning of package state: every answer on the affected addresses is the one refusal, sent after the body is read, on both faces. The disabled address moves into the class the unarmed address is already in, the class it joins after the re-sync. No new sender-visible distinction; no security-class finding, so no mechanism file is written.
- A post admitted just before the disable, or already queued: still `202` and still skipped at fire time. The fire-time skip stays, so nothing runs for a disabled package.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — The door's own `warn` line for this refusal states a cause that is not the true one: `unadmitted-address` says the qualifier does not name the package that ships the flow (it does), and `unknown-flow` says no hook is armed (one is), and both say the line is the only record of the cause. The true cause is the engine's `info` line, so a log read at `warn` shows the wrong diagnosis. The same generic lines are what the address logs after the re-sync, the wire answer is unaffected, and the ruling's "cause logged, never sent" is met. The comments in `trigger-api/src/plugin.ts:20-24` and `runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts` that say `undefined` covers every unshared name are stale for the same reason. Fix belongs to a follow-up card (a `disabled-holder` member of `UnverifiedPostCause` and the runtime door text); none is filed.

N2 (nit) — The `inboundHookSlot` jsdoc says no post is accepted whose run `triggerRun` would then skip. A post admitted just before the disable is still skipped at fire time. Accepted deviation; the code is correct.

N3 (nit) — The engine's line also fires for an address that would be refused with the package enabled (a wrong namespace on a disabled sole holder), and its text speaks of redelivery after the enable. Log wording only; accepted deviation.

**What I checked:**

It uses the same `isDisabledHolderSlot` predicate with the same argument order. The shared-name check runs after the qualified address picks its one key, so no co-holder is served in its place. - **Both faces.** All three callers of `inboundHookSlot` are unchanged. Each one reads the body in full and then answers the one `401 INVALID_SIGNATURE`, the same bytes the address gets after the re-sync, with nothing enqueued. Nothing sender-visible names the package, the namespace or the disabled state.
- **Re-enable.** The question is asked at post time with nothing cached, so the address answers `202` again with no re-arm.
- **Declarations.**
  - `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the right arm: the answer for the affected addresses moves from `202` to `401`.
  - `patch` with `!` and the BREAKING banner is right for `Metadata-protocol: none` under AGENTS.md step 3.
  - ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is right, because nothing durable moves.
  - The Skills-docs follow-up is carried by #34279.
- **Checks:** 52 check-runs, 36 success and 16 skipped, none red; `mergeable_state: clean`.
  - The new dogfood pin file runs on the queue and on push, never on a pull request, so no check-run on this head has executed it yet. Its green reading so far is the area's local battery. The merge queue is its first CI run.

**Follow-up owed (N1, needs a card):** the door's own `warn` line for this refusal names a generic cause (`unadmitted-address` / `unknown-flow`) that is not the true one; the true cause is only in the engine's `info` line. Two comments are stale for the same reason: `trigger-api/src/plugin.ts:20-24` and the one in `runtime/src/domains/automation-hooks.ts` both say `undefined` covers every unshared name. The fix is a `disabled-holder` member of `UnverifiedPostCause` and the runtime door text. Please file that card; no head moves.

**Accepted nits:**
- N2: the jsdoc says no post is accepted whose run is then skipped, but a post admitted just before the disable is still skipped at fire time. The code is correct.
- N3: the engine's line also fires for a wrong-namespace address of a disabled sole holder. This is log wording only.

Not governed: the area lands this PR per `landing-operations.md`.
